opus.why: Video title list for an audience. Sonnet writes punchy curiosity and blunt titles under a length limit just as well as a bigger model.

fable.why: Video titles are audience-facing hooks with a hard char limit and two tonal modes; Sonnet writes punchy titles reliably, Haiku tends toward generic ones.

opus.why: Feature names that have to sound right in both English and Russian. The bilingual phonetics need care, but it's a short naming task that Sonnet at high effort handles.

fable.why: Short feature names that must read well in both English and Russian need bilingual ear; Sonnet handles this, Haiku would produce awkward transliterations.

opus.why: Scroll-stopping first lines the audience will read: 12 hooks in three set styles, with clear source material. The craft matters, but Sonnet at high effort matches quality here.

fable.why: Scroll-stopping first lines for a client brand in three distinct vibes; audience-read copy but short and well-constrained, Sonnet matches Opus here.

opus.why: 20 everyday dilemma episode ideas, each with a one-line click reason, for a well-defined format. This is volume ideation, which suits Sonnet.

fable.why: 20 non-repetitive, click-worthy dilemmas plus audience rationale for each; the complaint is sameness, and Sonnet lists drift samey at this length, Opus keeps variety and taste.

opus.why: Brand book taglines with a careful tone that must avoid clichés, plus picking and defending a top 3. This is brand judgment, where a drop in quality shows.

fable.why: Brand-book taglines with explicit anti-cliché constraint and a reasoned top-3 pick; tagline quality and brand judgment show the model gap most clearly.

opus.why: The first try was rejected as the same angle reworded. Truly contrarian, argument-provoking angles need sharper originality than the first attempt had.

fable.why: Follow-up after a samey first attempt; genuinely contrarian angles that provoke argument need real taste, which is where the previous tier failed.

opus.why: Short names for an internal CLI. Low stakes and simple, but 'not cringe' needs some taste.

fable.why: Internal CLI name ideas with a 'not cringe' filter; low stakes, nobody external reads it, Sonnet at medium gives decent taste cheaply.

opus.why: A product positioning pivot: several angles, product names and hero lines, plus an honest call on which angle is strongest. Strategic brand judgment where quality matters most.

fable.why: Product positioning pivot: multiple angles, names, hero lines, plus an honest call on the strongest; strategy and brand judgment combined, Sonnet tends to praise everything.

opus.why: Opening hooks and a deck title for a client pitch, built from a clear outline with stats. Sonnet at high effort writes strong hooks from material this concrete.

fable.why: Six opening hooks and a deck title grounded in a given outline with concrete stats; well-scoped audience copy that Sonnet does at Opus level.
